The Kadapa Basin (Cuddapah Basin) is the oldest geological basin in Andhra Pradesh and one of the oldest sedimentary basins in India. Which of the following are the evidence of the phenomenon of continental drift?
I. The belt of ancient rocks from Brazil coast matches with those from Western Africa.
II. The gold deposits of Ghana are derived from the Brazil plateau when the two continents lay side by side.
III. The Gondwana system of sediments from India is known to have its counterparts in six different landmasses of the Southern Hemisphere.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Radiometric dating has shown that both the eastern coast of Brazil and the coastal belt of West Africa contain a strip of very ancient rocks about 2,000 million years old, of the same age and similar nature. The relationship between Ghana’s gold deposits and the source rocks of the Brazilian Plateau is also considered a classic piece of evidence for continental drift. The Gondwana sequence, based on sedimentary rocks derived from glacial deposits, is found across several continents of the Southern Hemisphere, including India, in almost the same thickness, composition, and order. This indicates that these landmasses were once parts of a single supercontinent, Gondwanaland. Therefore, all three statements I, II and III are correct, and the correct option is (c).

The process that continually adds new crust is:
x: The process that continually adds new crust is seafloor spreading. Significantly, new crust is created by seafloor spreading. Old crust is destroyed by subduction. It is important to mention here that the two factors roughly balance each other. So the shape and diameter of the Earth remain unchanged. Spreading seafloors are only an aspect of plate tectonics, another is subduction.
